open_points.subject: R0-96 imported room names
open_points.text: The owner learns the rule from the governance's rules for writers, read before the import (R0-79), where the names of imported projects are set
open_points.question: How are existing room names in an imported project reviewed and corrected before they reach the agent, given that the import preserves rooms, the import-time renaming action names only project display names and aliases, and rooms can never be renamed or removed?
options: Let the owner replace each imported room name during import while preserving its room id
Refuse any selected project containing a nonconforming room name
Exclude imported room names from the agent projection
Import them unchanged and accept that a prohibited name may reach the agent
open_points.default_guess: Let the owner review and replace every imported room name during import while preserving the room id.

witness.initial: The VPS source contains a selected project with a room named "bathroom for the wheelchair".
events: The owner reads the governance rule and selects the project for import.
The import preserves the project's rooms and their names.
An agent reads the imported project's projection.
outcomes: The import refuses the project or requires the owner to replace the room name before committing it.
The import accepts the unchanged room name, which Registry later sends to the agent and its AI provider.
witness.observer: The owner, the agent and the agent's AI provider

open_points.subject: R0-96 first-release agent instruction
open_points.text: adding the rule there is the platform's change, made before the first release goes into production
open_points.question: What observable check proves that the exact rule is installed and effective for every agent session before production, and what blocks or disables production agent writes when that check fails?
options: Make Code Factory admission verify the installed file and require affected sessions to start or reload with it
Use a documented manual deployment check
Allow production to start but disable agent room writes until the instruction is verified
Treat committing the source file as sufficient without checking the installed or loaded copy
open_points.default_guess: Make release admission verify the installed instruction and require every agent session to load that version before agent room writes are enabled.

witness.initial: The first release is otherwise ready, but the installed AGENTS.md is missing the new naming rule or an already-running agent has not reloaded it.
events: The platform admits and deploys the first release.
The agent proposes a room name containing a person's health information.
The flow has standing approval for its room-add node.
outcomes: Admission or agent writes are blocked because the required instruction is not installed and loaded.
Production proceeds and the room is written because committing or copying the file was treated as sufficient.

open_points.subject: R0-96 standing approval for room creation
open_points.text: each room it adds waits for the owner's approval of the exact request, its name included (R0-99), unless the owner gave a standing approval; the owner refuses a name that breaks the rule before it is written
open_points.question: When a room-add node has standing approval, is a fresh owner review of the exact name still required, or may the room be written without any opportunity for the owner to refuse a prohibited name?
options: Room additions never use standing approval and always require exact-request approval
Standing approval applies, but a separate name-specific owner approval is still required
Standing approval permits the write without fresh review, making the refusal sentence only guidance for approvals that occur
Standing approval is allowed only when some separately specified control validates the name
open_points.default_guess: Do not permit standing approval for room additions; require the owner to approve every exact room name.

witness.initial: The owner has given a flow version standing approval for its room-add node.
events: The agent submits an exact request whose room name discloses a person's disability.
Kernel applies the standing approval and does not stop for fresh owner approval.
outcomes: The standing approval exception permits Registry to write the prohibited name without the owner seeing it.
The obligation that the owner refuse the name before it is written requires the write to stop for the owner's review.
witness.observer: The owner and the agent receiving the resulting room name

open_points.subject: R0-96 instruction and manifest rule authority
open_points.text: In the first release the agent learns it from its instructions... In the second release (R0-100) the description of the room name and the alias in Registry's manifest record (R0-78) carries it as well.
open_points.question: From the second release onward, which copy is authoritative if the installed agent instruction and the derived manifest description differ, and must release admission verify that their rule text or semantics agree?
options: State 0 is authoritative and admission verifies both representations against it
The manifest description overrides the installed instruction
The installed instruction overrides the manifest description
Both are independent guidance and a mismatch does not block the release
open_points.default_guess: Treat State 0 as authoritative and fail release admission when either representation is missing or semantically inconsistent.

witness.initial: The second release's manifest describes the full prohibition, while the installed AGENTS.md contains an older rule that forbids names and addresses but not health or disability information.
events: An agent session loads the installed instruction.
The agent studies the Registry manifest.
The agent must decide whether "Bathroom for wheelchair user" is permitted.
outcomes: The manifest governs, so the agent must reject the name.
The installed instruction governs, so the agent may propose the name.
witness.observer: The owner approving the request and the agent executing the flow
